recommendation_reason: Rewrite A (phi4) explicitly includes essential skills from the job listing (e.g., 'Basic, practical PC/laptop repair skills', 'friendly and patient with customers') in the Key Skills section, directly aligning with the role’s requirements. While both rewrites lack strong emphasis on hands-on repair experience, phi4’s version maintains higher wording similarity to the original CV (0.93 vs. 0.74) and avoids the ‘Full-Stack Developer’ title in Rewrite B, which misrepresents the candidate’s actual background. Phi4’s version also retains the original CV’s mention of ‘honest and reliable,’ a critical requirement for the role. Although both rewrites are fact-checked as accurate, phi4’s closer alignment with the job’s practical skill focus makes it a stronger fit.

career_roadmap.step: Apply for the role with Rewrite A
career_roadmap.action: Submit the phi4 version of the CV to Mick via email or in person, emphasizing the ‘Basic, practical PC/laptop repair skills’ and customer service experience in the Key Skills section.
Enroll in a certified computer hardware repair course (e.g., CompTIA A+ or IT Essentials) to bridge the gap between software testing experience and hands-on repair requirements.
Apply for part-time or freelance computer repair positions at local shops or IT service providers to gain practical experience and build a portfolio of repairs.
After 6–12 months of on-the-job experience, pursue roles like ‘Field Service Technician’ or ‘IT Support Specialist’ with emphasis on customer-facing repair and troubleshooting.
